key_insight: Geo-Align uses a metric-geometry-based reward to align generated videos to real-world camera motion and physical scale, enabling accurate camera-controlled re-rendering without requiring synchronized multi-view training data.
problem_solved: Current video-to-video re-rendering relies on supervised fine-tuning with synthetic multi-view datasets, which are scarce for real-world scenes; as a result, models generalize poorly to out-of-distribution videos and fail to respect true camera motion and scale.
method: Define a geometry-aware reward that measures alignment between generated frames and real-world geometric cues (e.g., relative camera motion, scale consistency, and structure implied by depth/flow/SfM estimates).

Use the metric-geometry reward to guide optimization (reward-weighted fine-tuning or policy gradients) of an existing video generation model, removing dependence on paired/synchronized multi-view data.
Leverage monocular geometric signals (optical flow, inferred depth or SfM poses) from real videos as weak supervision for camera and scale alignment during training.
impact: By providing a self-supervised, geometry-driven training signal, Geo-Align improves realism and physical correctness of camera-controlled video generation, reducing reliance on synthetic datasets and improving robustness on real-world inputs—beneficial for AR/VR, robotics, and content creation workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input real video -> geometric cue extraction (depth/flow/SfM) -> metric-geometry reward -> model fine-tuning loop

paper_title: Geo-Align: Video Generation Alignment via Metric Geometry Reward
paper_authors: Zizun Li, Haoyu Guo, Runzhe Teng, Chunhua Shen, Tong He
